text:
lily_pr: Heads-up: NYT just ran a mention of our Optimize toolkit and quoted "up to 40% cost reduction" in the headline. Our published average is 34% and the "up to" framing is fine for product marketing, but the headline presents it as typical. Need PR + eng to decide if we request a headline edit. :thinking_face:

dan_engineering: Confirming — the 34% is the mean across our customer evals; 40% was the maximum observed in one specific workload. We should ask for clarity in the headline (change to "average ~34%" or similar).

jasmin_marketing: If NYT changes the headline we should coordinate a short clarification tweet and update our benchmark landing page with a highlighted note so partners don't reshare the inflated stat.

lily_pr: Agreed. I'll draft a correction note to the reporter (byline contact in article) proposing: "Suggested headline clarification: 'Redwood Optimize reduces inference costs by an average of ~34%; peak savings observed up to 40% on select workloads.'" Keep short and factual.

tom_sales: Also flagging Sales: we had a handful of outreach emails with the 40% callout this morning. Can we get an internal 1-paragraph to forward to prospects so reps use the precise language?

olivia_ops: If we share any backend logs or artifacts with the reporter for substantiation, I can scrub hostnames and account IDs. We should avoid sharing customer-identifying data.

reed_ceo: Good approach. Keep the tone collaborative. Offer the methodology appendix and a small visual if they want to update the piece. We should not make it adversarial.

lily_pr: Draft email: "Hi Alex — thanks for covering Redwood's Optimize toolkit. Quick suggestion to clarify the headline to reflect our aggregated results: 'reduces inference costs by an average of ~34%; peak savings observed up to 40% on specific workloads.' We're happy to share a redacted methodology appendix and the small chart you can paste. Best, Lily (PR)."

dan_engineering: LGTM. Attaching the redacted results table to the secure share (internal link).

press_bot: reporter_email_delivered: true

lily_pr: Alex replied: "Thanks — will discuss with the editor and aim for a headline tweak. Could you paste the one-line clarification we can use?" I've pasted the suggested headline above.

jasmin_marketing: Preparing the internal sales blurb now. Proposed copy: "Clarification: Our benchmark shows an average ~34% cost reduction using Redwood Optimize; peak savings up to 40% on certain workloads. See methodology in the public report." Will drop in #sales in 10m.

olivia_ops: Confirmed scrubbed files used. Sent link to Lily for reporter attachment.

press_bot: article_update_detected: https://www.nytimes.com/example-corrected

lily_pr: NYT updated the headline to: "Redwood Optimize cuts inference costs by an average of about 34%" and appended an editor's note referencing our methodology. Link above.

jasmin_marketing: Posted clarification to our social channels and updated the benchmark landing page with an editor's note. Also pushed the 1-paragraph to #sales and pinned the new deck slide.

tom_sales: Got the note — sharing with prospects now. Thanks for the speedy turnaround.

reed_ceo: Nice work all. Please save artifacts for the postmortem and mark any partners who already syndicated the old headline so we can nudge them.

lily_pr: Loop closed. Saved the email thread and assets in the comms drive, and added a short postmortem checklist entry to avoid percentile/peak confusion in future outreach. If anyone spots further syndication of the 40% headline, tag me. :white_check_mark:
